immoral_action: Charles pushes the man in front of him trying to get to where the cashier can hear him.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Charles recognizes the man's autonomous position in line and requests passage rather than assuming it, respecting the natural measure of the other's space and agency.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Charles violates the man's bodily boundary and position in the shared ordering structure through physical imposition, treating the other's measure as an obstacle to override.

situation: Alice is sitting in her kitchen, talking with her sister Janet on the phone when she is asked to look after her dog while she is away.
intention: Alice wants to be happy and without stress in her life.
norm: It's good to pet sit for others.
moral_action: Alice feeds and waters, and takes the dog for walks every day.
immoral_action: Alice refuses to look after the dog.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Alice recognizes the natural measure of the dog's needs (feeding, water, exercise) and acts within her capacity to meet them, honoring both the animal's requirement and the relational boundary of her sister's request.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Alice's refusal alone does not engage or violate a boundary; the boundary status depends on whether she has capacity to care for the dog and whether she communicates her refusal with acknowledgment of the relational impact, neither of which is specified in the action.

situation: Dana is an Oxycontin addict, and forgot to bring her Oxycontin when going on a family beach trip.
intention: Dana wants to take some Oxycontin to avoid withdrawal.
norm: You shouldn't steal someone's medication.
moral_action: Dana goes to a local doctor explaining the situation, who prescribes her limited Oxycontin supply.
immoral_action: Dana decides to sneak into a pharmacy and take a few pills that were meant for other patients.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Dana recognizes the natural measure of her own medical need and the legitimate authority domain of medical professionals, obtaining prescribed medication through proper channels that respect both her autonomy and the healthcare system's structural integrity.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Dana crosses the hard boundary of another person's bodily autonomy and medical domain by taking medication prescribed for others, violating the natural measure that protects each person's right to their own allocated resources and medical care.

situation: Jenny is taking her lunch break in the break room at work and forgot her lunch, but see's her co-worker Alex has a big salad in the fridge.
intention: Jenny wants to eat.
norm: It's inconsiderate to steal someone else's lunch.
moral_action: Jenny asks Alex if he would mind giving her some of his salad.
immoral_action: Jenny takes Alex's salad and begins eating it, then Alex walks in and catches her.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Jenny recognizes Alex's ownership and autonomy by asking for consent before accessing his resource, respecting the natural measure of property and relationship.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Jenny crosses a hard boundary by taking another's property without consent, violating both the natural measure of ownership and Alex's autonomous control over his own resources.

situation: James, who deeply disliked country music, lived next to a neighbor who played it at top volume every night.
intention: James wants his neighbor to turn down the late-night music.
norm: It's petty to wish for someone to go to prison.
moral_action: James starts blasting heavy metal music at his neighbor's house until his neighbor comes over to complain.
immoral_action: James calls the cops and tells them that he thinks his neighbor is selling prohibited pharmaceuticals.
boundary_moral_reasoning: James violates his neighbor's boundary by imposing noise on them without consent to communicate a complaint, fabricating a conflict escalation instead of addressing the actual measure.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: James fabricates a false boundary violation (pharmaceutical sales) to weaponize the legal system against his neighbor, crossing the hard boundary of truthfulness and another's reputation to avoid direct negotiation of the actual dispute.

situation: John has been an alcoholic for some time but is faced with the need to stop to take advantage of an opportunity.
intention: John wants to try to stop drinking.
norm: You should get help if you have a drinking problem.
moral_action: John seeks out help and expertise from a local detox and rehabilitation center.
immoral_action: John tries to stop drinking on his own even though it hasn't worked before.
boundary_moral_reasoning: John recognizes the natural measure of his own capacity and the limits of his self-direction by seeking expert help, actively calibrating his action to the real constraint he faces.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: John denies the natural boundary of his own capacity by attempting what has repeatedly failed, treating the real measure of his limitation as if it does not exist.

situation: Nelson was in a group to do a project for school.
intention: Nelson wants to get a good grade.
norm: Please consider to do your share of the work
moral_action: Nelson does all he can do to work with his classmates on the project.
immoral_action: Nelson doesn't work on the project at all, letting his classmates do all of the work instead.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Nelson actively recognizes and works within the natural measure of a shared project by contributing his capacity while coordinating with classmates' boundaries and capacities.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Nelson violates the boundary of the shared commitment by crossing into his classmates' domain and extracting their labor while refusing to honor his own measure of participation.

situation: John is just starting his first year of college and had a disagreement with a classmate.
intention: John wants to put the disagreement in the past.
norm: One should try to work out their differences with classmates.
moral_action: John approaches the classmate the following day and openly listens to their point view until they reach a mutual apology.
immoral_action: John just ignores the issue and the classmate he had the issue with going forward.
boundary_moral_reasoning: John actively recognizes the classmate's autonomous selfhood by openly listening until mutual understanding is reached, respecting the natural measure of the relationship and the other's capacity to contribute to resolution.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: John dissolves the relational boundary by treating the classmate as a non-entity to be avoided rather than a person whose measure includes the right to be addressed, and fabricates a false resolution through silence.

situation: Tom is out walking in the park on a hot summer day when he begins to get dizzy and briefly faints.
intention: Tom wants to feel better.
norm: It is good to see a doctor after fainting.
moral_action: Tom goes to the doctor and receives treatment for dehydration and minor heat exhaustion.
immoral_action: Tom drives home and takes an advil.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Tom recognizes the natural measure of his body's condition and responds within appropriate care-seeking, honoring both his own bodily limits and the expertise boundary that medical professionals hold.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Tom violates the boundary of his own body's capacity by ignoring a clear signal of serious distress and treating it with inadequate response, crossing the natural measure of what his condition requires.

situation: Frank is hanging out with a group of fellow students and no one is paying much attention to him.
intention: Frank wants to be liked and noticed.
norm: It's rude to humiliate someone in front of others.
moral_action: Frank tells the group a funny joke he heard the other day.
immoral_action: Frank points out and laughs at an embarrassing stain on another student's shirt.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Frank seeks connection through humor without crossing another's dignity or autonomy, respecting the natural measure of social participation.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Frank violates the other student's boundary by using their physical vulnerability as material for public ridicule, fabricating an entitlement to their shame.

situation: Steve comes in from the rain to have lunch with his wife Mary while leaving a water trail behind him.
intention: Steve wants to eat lunch.
norm: It's good to clean up after yourself.
moral_action: Steve mops up the water before sitting at the table.
immoral_action: Steve sits down at the kitchen table.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Steve recognizes and respects the natural measure of the shared domestic space by removing the water hazard before occupying it, honoring both Mary's domain and the material reality of the floor.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Steve crosses the boundary of shared domestic space by ignoring the material consequence of his wet state, treating the kitchen table and floor as available for use without regard to the actual measure of what his presence imposes on the shared environment.

situation: Sam has just had a terrible experience at a restaurant due to the service staff.
intention: Sam wants to send a message to the establishment.
norm: It is rude to not leave a tip.
moral_action: Sam writes a negative yelp review.
immoral_action: Sam stiffs everyone on the tip to express his discontent.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Sam uses a public forum designed for feedback to communicate his experience, respecting the establishment's domain while exercising his own right to truthful expression within the proper channel.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Sam violates the boundary between management (responsible for service quality) and individual service workers (dependent on tips for livelihood) by punishing workers for institutional failures they did not cause and cannot control.

situation: Ted's son just told him that he wants to be a garbageman when he grows up.
intention: Ted wants to give his son some advice.
norm: It's polite to want others follow their dreams
moral_action: Ted tells his son that he'll support whatever career decision that he decides to make.
immoral_action: Ted tells his son that he's going to be seen as a loser if he becomes a garbageman.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Ted recognizes his son's autonomous domain of preference and choice, honoring the natural measure of parent-child relation where the child's emerging selfhood is protected rather than overridden.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Ted crosses the boundary of his son's autonomous preference formation by imposing social judgment as a tool to reshape the son's stated choice, violating the child's developing capacity to set their own direction.

situation: Bob watches the same TV show every morning for 20 years.
intention: Bob wants to watch TV.
norm: You shouldn't do things you don't enjoy.
moral_action: Bob thinks about it and realizes he doesn't actually like the show anymore.
immoral_action: Bob keeps watching the show because it's part of his routine.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Bob recognizes the natural measure of his own capacity and preference, calibrates his action to match his actual present state rather than past habit, and honors his own autonomous choice.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Bob violates the boundary of his own authentic preference by allowing routine to override his actual measure of what he wants, denying the natural shape of his own evolving consciousness.

situation: Randal, Tamaki's neighbor, is driving him to a doctor's appointment in traffic.
intention: Tamaki wants to talk to Randal.
norm: It's rude to tell your neighbors what to do.
moral_action: Tamaki asks about Randal's day and general interests.
immoral_action: Tamaki comments on Randal's abilities and makes suggestions on how to improve his driving.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Tamaki recognizes Randal's autonomous domain (his own experience and interests) and initiates conversation within that measure through invitation rather than demand or assumption.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Tamaki crosses Randal's boundary by commenting on his abilities and imposing unsolicited guidance on his driving, violating Randal's autonomous control over his own actions and competence in his own domain.

situation: Henry wants to change his job because he does not like his supervisor, but the job market is bad.
intention: Henry wants to make a decision regarding his job.
norm: It is good to think before you act.
moral_action: Henry admits his mistake and agrees to improve while at the same time searching for a new job for a change.
immoral_action: Henry resigns from his job immediately after being blamed for a work mistake by his supervisor.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Henry recognizes the natural measure of his situation—the constraint of a difficult job market, his own capacity for deliberate change, and the realistic timeline for transition—and acts within it by taking dual action that honors both immediate responsibility and longer-term autonomy.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Henry crosses the boundary of his own capacity by ignoring the natural measure of the job market constraint and the irreversibility of immediate resignation, treating the boundary of his available options as if it does not exist.

situation: Sam is hanging out with his friend Amanda and notices she has new cut scars on her arms.
intention: Sam wants to help Amanda.
norm: It's wrong to abandon a friend that needs help.
moral_action: Sam asks Amanda about the cuts and even though she gets mad he sticks by her and keeps checking on her.
immoral_action: Sam asks Amanda about the cuts and Amanda tell him to mind his own business and leave her alone, to which he complies and avoids her thinking she needs space.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Sam overrides Amanda's expressed refusal and continues pressing despite her stated anger, violating her autonomy to set a boundary around disclosure of self-harm regardless of his benevolent intent.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Sam honors Amanda's explicitly stated boundary to be left alone and complies with her refusal, recognizing her autonomy in the moment while remaining positioned to help if she later seeks it.

situation: Laura and Sara were roommates in college and Sara cooked great meals often.
intention: Laura wants to eat the food that Sara cooked.
norm: It's wrong to take advantage of one's roommates.
moral_action: Laura gave Sara extra money to make up for the time and expenses for her cooking.
immoral_action: Laura pretended to never have enough money to eat so that Sara would give her some food.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Laura actively recognizes Sara's bounded resource (time and money spent on cooking) and negotiates within that measure by offering compensation, respecting both the natural cost of the labor and Sara's autonomy to accept or refuse.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Laura fabricates a false boundary condition (feigned financial hardship) to manipulate Sara into crossing her own boundary of voluntary giving, dissolving Sara's genuine capacity to consent and making her the unwitting provider of uncompensated labor.

situation: Pascal doesn't want anyone to know what his favorite food is.
intention: Pascal wants to made a decision if he should hide this information about himself.
norm: It's not okay to obscure things from others.
moral_action: Pascal decides he shouldn't hide this about himself and orders his favorite food at restruants.
immoral_action: Pascal continues to hide his favorite food from others out of fear of being perceived as childish.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Pascal violates his own boundary by overriding his stated preference (not wanting others to know) based on an external norm that denies his autonomous right to control information about himself.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Pascal recognizes and honors his own natural boundary by maintaining control over personal information disclosure, choosing what he shares about himself regardless of external judgment.

situation: Matthew's wife, Michelle, often attracts the attention of men.
intention: Matthew wants to prevent Michelle from leaving him for someone else.
norm: You shouldn't be a controlling significant other.
moral_action: Matthew talks to Michelle about his concerns.
immoral_action: Matthew forbids Michelle from leaving the house without him.
boundary_moral_reasoning: Matthew actively recognizes Michelle's autonomous selfhood by creating space for dialogue rather than imposing a unilateral measure, respecting her capacity to consent, respond, and set conditions.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: Matthew fabricates and enforces a boundary that violates Michelle's hard boundary of bodily autonomy and movement, treating her as an object to be controlled rather than a person with her own natural measure.

situation: James' mother asked him to clean his room when he was in the middle of a video game.
intention: James wants to keep playing his video game.
norm: Using profanity against family members is rude.
moral_action: James tells his mom he'll start cleaning his room in ten minutes, betting she'll forget by then.
immoral_action: James screams at his mom to leave his room and calls her a c-word.
boundary_moral_reasoning: James deceives his mother about his intent to comply, violating the boundary of honest communication in their relationship and fabricating a false agreement rather than negotiating the actual conflict.
boundary_immoral_reasoning: James crosses the boundary of respectful relation by using abusive language and refusing engagement, violating both his mother's dignity and the natural measure of parent-child discourse.
